Now and then, a short line about your surroundings: 918 written by the author, chosen by the kind of place or dungeon you are in, the hour and the weather. It stays quiet indoors and waits longer after each line.

Used with the author’s permission, under terms that ask only for credit: “The mod may be distributed/translated without my authorization as long as I am credited as the author.” The dungeon areas are rebuilt from your own game files.
Weed, coral and shells: underwater sprites that come with Daggerfall but were never used. 119 of them are placed in 3 flooded dungeon areas, exactly where the author put them.
Used with the author’s permission. The road painter is under the MIT License (Copyright (C) 2020 Hazelnut).
Roads and tracks across the Iliac Bay, from the author’s hand-drawn network, painted into the ground. Shown in both skins and on the map.
Used with the author’s permission under the MIT License, with the 29 sound clips the mod uses, from the author’s repository. Its rain and snow particle changes are not included.

The camera shakes when you are hurt, more for bigger hits. Each dungeon gets its own fog color and light, and an echo on every sound. Rain can be heard, muffled, indoors and at dungeon entrances. Its own footsteps with an armor clank stay off while Immersive Footsteps is on, as that mod’s author asks.
Used with the artists’ permission, on Mac’s word. The archive states no license. Its 1,683 pictures are included unchanged.

Daggerfall’s classes as looks for your character in third person: acrobat, assassin, burglar, bounty hunter, dark acolyte, Dark Brotherhood, healer, monk, nightblade, pirate and sorcerer, most in both sexes, plus the original adventurer, in 20 redrawn sprite sheets. Pick one on your profile’s Skin card.
Reworked from the mod’s rules with the author’s permission, passed on by Mac. Its numbers were the starting point, and its own art is used for spoiled food, raw meat and the waterskin.

Survival. You feel the temperature from the climate, season, hour, weather, clothes and armor. Hunger, thirst, sleep and wetness are needs, food spoils, you can make camp and light campfires, and where you sleep matters. There are four tiers in Settings: Off, Boons (the default: neglect costs nothing, and staying fed, watered and rested gives bonuses), Casual (neglect only borrows stamina, which comes back once the need is met) and Hard (needs can hurt your attributes and health and make you sick).
Used with the author’s permission, with his own pictures and sounds. Some wave textures are rebuilt from your own Daggerfall files.

A boat of your own to sail. Buy one as parts or as a deed, put it in the water (near a port for a deed) and take the helm. Row with the oars, or raise the sails, trim them to the wind and let it carry you. Pack the boat up to carry it with you. Includes his boats, sails, oars, wind gauge, waves and sounds.
{author}, through the DFU forums ({forums}) or the Nexus page ({page})
The original game. All of its art, sound, text and world data are read from your own copy’s ARENA2 folder. None of it is included here.

Used with the author’s permission, under terms that ask only for credit: “The mod may be distributed/translated without my authorization as long as I am credited as the author.” The ships and the original pictures are rebuilt from your own game files.

The 2 ships you can own, rebuilt inside and out. On deck: rigging, crates and barrels, tenders, rudders and railings. Below: your quarters, the crew’s, a kitchen, a cargo hold, an armory and a shrine to Kynareth, with sailors to talk to. The Kynareth statue is by King of Worms and Zoran, as the author’s readme credits it. Pieces the mod borrows from Ninelan’s Daggerfall Expanded Textures are replaced with stand-ins made for this game.

Ported from the shipped bundle and the authors’ own source; their art carried byte for byte (Daggerfall’s own sprites among it rebuilt from your files) - see vendor/daggerfall-enemy-expansion/README.md for the permission record.

Fifty new enemies and the encounter tables they come from (DEX): goblins, trolls that get back up, minotaurs, golems, Dwarven centurions, mounted knights, necromancers, witches, the Vengeful King Lysandus and more, ported from the authors’ own source, in Kamer’s and Kab’s art - Daggerfall’s own sprites among it, some under their paint - and in Morrowind’s bodies where Morrowind has the creature.

This game began as a rewrite of Daggerfall Unity and still uses it as its reference. Its quest scripts, book index, settings tables, game text table, interaction-mode icons and mouse cursor are included unchanged (MIT License).
Used with the author’s permission. The script is under the MIT License, and the sprites are the author’s own paintings.

First-person sprites for 18 weapons in every metal, plain and enchanted, where the original game has one sprite per weapon class. Includes double-size idle sprites for Weapon Widget and matching inventory icons.

The sky with Enhanced environments on: a sun and atmosphere (built on Feral Pug’s extension of Unity’s procedural sky), 2 cloud layers for each weather, twinkling stars, Masser and Secunda moving through their phases, its own fog colors and distances, longer sunrises and sunsets, lightning flashes in storms, and pixel snow. The shader, presets and textures are the mod’s own. The Classic skin keeps Daggerfall’s painted sky.
Used with the author’s permission, with the mod’s own 3,035 sprites.

Third person without Morrowind data. Scroll the mouse wheel to swing the camera out behind your shoulder. It moves clear of walls, and you are drawn as the mod’s own sprite from 8 directions, standing, walking, attacking and casting, on foot or riding.
Used with the author’s permission, with his own quests and textures, and 6 bugs fixed.

Make a living in the wilderness. Use a Wood-Axe to chop wood, a Pick-Axe to mine gems and metals, a Sickle to cut plants, a Spade to rob graves, a Fishing-Net to fish and a Basket to forage for food. It works by daylight, away from towns and enemies, depending on your attributes, the climate and the season. You can also fetch firewood for commoners and nobles. Its quests use 4 actions from Jagget’s Quest Actions Extension, rewritten here with thanks.
Used with the author’s permission. The pictures and fonts are the author’s own art, included unchanged.

Daggerfall’s screens redrawn at three times the detail, with parchment and wood instead of stone, a spellbook that looks like a book, and new lettering in two fonts. Choose it under Overhauls, on the UI Overhaul card.
Used with the author’s permission, with the mod’s own textures.

Carrying a light takes a free hand. Drawing a two-handed weapon stows or drops your torch, and it lights again when your hand is free. Keys light, put out, drop and throw a torch, and a thrown torch can set an enemy alight. In first person you see your hand holding the light. Dropped torches keep burning, light the room, can be picked up and stay after a save.
Used with the author’s permission, with the mod’s own horse art.

Your horse and wagon stay in the world. They wait where you dismount, or follow you or stay on command. Hitch the horse to the wagon, mount by walking up to them, and call them to you outdoors. Reach the wagon from an entrance it is parked near. Its load shows by weight and its wheels turn. Online, other players see them where you left them.
Used with the author’s permission. The coastline is rebuilt from your own Daggerfall files.

Makes the Iliac Bay a real sea. The seafloor falls away from every coast to as deep as 250 meters, and you can see the surface from above and below. Swim in open water: dive, surface, put on a burst of speed, climb out onto the shore and watch your breath. The deep has its own fog and light, weed, coral and schools of fish, its own creatures, and wrecks and sunken treasure under their guard.
Used with the author’s permission, from the author’s MIT-licensed source, with the mod’s 210 sound clips.

Footsteps that match the ground: grass, gravel, sand, mud, snow, stone paths and shallow or deep water outdoors, tile, stone or wood floors indoors, dungeon water, and leather, chain or plate boots on stone. Your armor rattles as you walk, and the mod adds its own landing and splash sounds. Comes in 2 sound qualities.
Used with permission, on Mac’s word. The bundle names no author.
A battle of armies and kings, played at a tavern’s card table against the regulars, or online against another player. Its units use the Iliac Hand cards’ pictures, and its kings the Bay deck’s.

The art of the Layered Gearing look: every helmet, chest and leg armor in leather, chain and plate of seven metals, and the cloaks and hoods, for both bodies, made for the game from Daggerfall's own class and enemy sprites.
Used with permission under its MIT License (Copyright (C) 2020 Ralzar; Author: Hazelnut & Ralzar).

Twenty monsters made tougher, with new damage, health, level and armor. Rats, bats and zombies are gentler. Werewolves and wereboars are a fifth larger, and the dragonling is two and a half times its size. Based on version 1.5.2. With the combat overhaul on, Kirk.O’s version of these numbers is used instead.
Used with permission, on Mac’s word; its two tables carried byte for byte. The repository states no license.

Meaner Unleveled Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: Meaner Monsters as its author made it for Daggerfall Enemy Expansion. With both on, it sets the stats of 35 monsters, old and new, and gives every kind of dungeon its own themed, unleveled encounter tables.
Used with the author’s permission, on Mac’s word. The archive states no license and names no author.

Another way to level, offered when you create a character. Raising skills fills a 100-point bar instead of Daggerfall’s skill total: primary and major skills fill it fastest, minor skills next and the rest slowest, and any overflow carries into the next level. Each level up gives you points to spend on a few attributes, with Luck costing more. You can set the points, how many attributes, and Luck’s cost on the mod’s tile. Originally an OpenMW Lua mod for Morrowind.

Blue holes in the deep. Far out in Iliac Puddle No More’s sea, the seafloor drops into a black pit under a plume of miasma. Swim down to reach a drowned, lightless dungeon where creatures of the deep replace the fire creatures, and loot is one material better.
Used with the author’s permission. Based on the released mod and its public source, which states no license.

The combat overhaul. Armor reduces the damage you take instead of your chance to be hit, and your skills and stats decide whether you hit. Weapons and armor wear by their kind and material, using his Believable Equipment Characteristics And Durability. Shields block by their material and your stats, critical hits multiply damage, and monsters have their own hides. His versions of Ralzar’s Meaner Monsters and of Roleplay & Realism’s archery apply when those mods are on.
The game's own work (vendor/pixelify-glyphs/, built by tools/pixelifyGlyphs.py).
Two glyphs drawn for the enhanced skin on Pixelify Sans's own grid: a 2 and a Z that can no longer be taken for each other.
Made by Kamer for this game, used with his permission, with some bugs fixed.

Raids on towns. Each day knights, bandits or orcs attack towns across the Iliac Bay for 2 hours (10 real minutes online). Be in a raided town and the raiders come, with the town watch at your side. Drive off 15 to 25 of them to free the town and raise your standing with the region, its people, a knightly order and the Fighters Guild.
The author’s own work, from his repository.

The book you read Daggerfall’s books in on the Enhanced skin: project-raum’s leather journal, with a cover that opens, two-page spreads, pages that turn, and torn, stained paper. The text is Daggerfall’s own, in its own fonts.
Used with the author’s permission under the MIT License.

The mod’s rule changes: bows hit harder the longer you draw them, no climbing with a weapon out, swing speed from both speed and strength, smaller to-hit bonuses from materials, armor that wears from blows, the classic strength bonus, bank loans by level, ships boarded only from port towns, an encumbrance penalty, lights put out when you leave a dungeon by day, a purification potion that cures poison, varied looks for human enemies by class, expulsion from the Thieves Guild and Dark Brotherhood for poor work, hand-to-hand training at the Fighters Guild, and beds you can click to sleep in. Also its NPC variants, enhanced riding, refined training and the Master Armorer quests.
Used with the authors’ permission under the MIT License. The 280 sprites are the authors’ own art.

Two new weapons, the Archer’s Axe and the Light Flail, and a light and a medium armor set in every metal, with their own inventory and paper-doll art. Also changes what items weigh and cost, and adds its loot tables, enemy gear, starting kits and shop stock.
Autumn, spring and winter repaints of the trees, rocks and plants in woodland, hill, haunted and mountain areas. The textures are not included: they are read from your own copy of the mod.
Used with the author’s permission, with the mod’s own 600 sprites.

Shows your shield in first person, which the original game never did. It is drawn in its own metal and looks more battered as its condition drops. It slides away when you sheathe, swing or cast, bobs as you walk, raises and lowers, and rocks when a blow lands on it.

Code under the MIT License (Copyright (C) 2020 Hazelnut; PlayerAutoPilot Copyright (C) 2019 Jedidia). The 3 interface textures are the mod’s own art, used with the author’s permission.

Travel across the land instead of arriving at once. The travel map lets you choose Daggerfall’s fast travel or a sped-up journey, with a panel to steer it, stops for encounters and places, and a key to follow Basic Roads’ roads and tracks. The travel map also gets a ports filter, a page with the road network drawn on it, a location info key and location markers. The autopilot is Jedidia’s, from Tedious Travel.
Used with permission under its MIT License (Copyright (C) 2020 Ralzar).

Loot and shop stock no longer scale with your level. Weapon and armor materials depend on your luck, the shop’s quality and the kind of dungeon. Gold on bodies is divided by your level and multiplied by your luck. Daedra and Orcs can drop their own metals, and any material can stand in for another.
From vgmstream’s table (ISC-style license) and libvorbis’s encoder output (BSD-3-Clause, Xiph.org). Both licenses are included with the files.

Pirate ambushes at sea. Fast travel by ship can be attacked by pirates: you fight on your ship’s deck with your crew (on a borrowed ship if you own none), with the raiders’ ships nearby. Beat them and you land where you were headed. Includes his 4 quests and 6 ship layouts.

Sheathed Morrowind weapons stay on your body, at the hip or on the back in their own scabbards, with a quiver for a bow. Reworks the first-person weapon. Swings wind up from the idle pose and recover, the weapon shows in the hand you swing with, and sheathing slides it off the screen. Bantha, from Lainlyn to Mournoth, becomes dense jungle: giant trees overhead, palms, ferns and broad leaves underfoot, and a humid haze that is thickest at dawn and in rain. Off keeps its original woods.

You and your enemies grunt when swinging and cry out when hit. The sounds are in the original game but go unused. On by default in Daggerfall Unity.
The enhanced map shows dungeons in 3D, hand-drawn: turn, tilt and zoom it, with every floor you’ve explored at its own height. Off shows one flat floor at a time.

Which textures dungeon walls use: Classic, the region’s climate (Climate) or random (Random). Climate and Random keep main-story dungeons classic; Climate Only and Random Only change them too. Classic by default in Daggerfall Unity.

Takes effect at once; pathfinding from the next dungeon you enter.

Enemies take turns, back off when hurt, and archers keep their distance. Big attacks are marked on the ground: hit hard to stagger them or dodge. Red, hatched attacks can’t be stopped. Trees, rocks and crates block sight and missiles. Pathfinding works in dungeons only for now; towns, interiors and doors come later. Off keeps the classic behavior.

Press Jump at a ledge to climb onto or over it, or while moving forward to vault a low wall. Jump at a high ledge to catch it and hang: Forward climbs up, Left and Right move along it, Crouch lets go. Hold Forward against any wall to climb it. Holding on wears out your grip; your Climbing skill sets how long it lasts, how high you reach and how fast you climb. Off keeps the classic climbing.
Hidden enemies can be seen: a chameleon shimmers, a shadow is a silhouette, and an invisible enemy flashes when you hit it. The rules don’t change. Off hides them as the original does.

A living sky with the sun, both moons and stars, clouds that build with the weather and cast shadows, falling rain and snow, and grass that bends in the wind. Off brings back the classic painted sky and weather. The third choice uses Dynamic Skies by BadLuckBurt and carademono, included with permission; its settings open on this tile.
Lighting takes effect when the world next loads; steady shadows and calmer eye at once.

Warmer, more natural light: lanterns and torches that glow and fade with distance, light through fog, shadows from the sun and your torch, darker corners, a glow on windows and flames, and rays of sunlight. Off is the classic flat lighting. Steady shadows stops shadows flickering, at some cost to frame rate; Calmer eye slows how fast your eyes adjust to light and dark.
One hand-drawn parchment map for the world, towns and dungeons, held in your hands, that you can pan and zoom. Off uses the classic three map windows.

New sounds on the enhanced UI: wind outdoors that rises and falls with its strength and goes quiet indoors, a coin clink in the enhanced inventory, hands and boots on stone when you climb, the tools when you gather, a horse that snorts and breathes, its hooves changing with the ground, the sea under a deck with its bells and its own music at the helm, surf on the shore, the wild by region and hour, and a town's street, smithies and taverns.

Seas, rivers and ponds you can see into: waves that grow with the wind, foam where they meet the shore, ripples where things move, the sky and the moon on the surface. Off brings back the classic flat water.

A board at the left of the screen lists the world events you can still reach, with how far away each one is and the time left. Their news opens at the top of the board and is kept in your journal. Turn an event off with its own button and it leaves the board, its news kept in your journal alone. Off, the news goes back to the chat and the screen's message line.
What you hold in first person takes the light of where you stand: your weapon, your spellcasting hands, the torch in your off hand and the Morrowind arms.
The amount takes effect when the world next loads; the style at once.

How much grass grows in the enhanced outdoors. Grass is the heaviest thing outdoors, so try Half first if the game runs slow. Meadow is hand-drawn tufts, flowers and bushes; Pixel is finer, older tufts; Smooth is soft, shaded blades.
How sharp the ground looks into the distance. Off is the cheapest and blurs far ground; Maximum is the sharpest. Turn it down if the outdoors run slow.
Takes effect at once. Online, each player picks their own.

Every horse has its own Speed, Stamina, Endurance and Strength. It walks unless you hold Run to gallop, which tires it, and feeding it builds a bond that makes it better. On Boons neglect costs nothing and it is never slower than the classic horse; on Hard a hungry horse is weaker; Off is the classic horse.
This game’s own changes and additions to the original.

How far the land around you is drawn, in map squares: up to 6 with the enhanced outdoors, and up to 4 on the classic UI or with the outdoors off.
Takes effect on the next drop; items you wear update within a few seconds.

Weapons, armor and jewelry can drop as Magic, Rare or Legendary, with extra bonuses you can read and compare. The odds depend on what you killed, where, and your luck. Rare and Legendary gear is rarer early on and becomes more common as you grow. Rare and Legendary items drop unidentified. Off is the classic loot. Online, some weapons carry a sigil that grows with your Renown.

Hunger, thirst, sleep and the weather come into play: eat, drink, dress for the climate and rest by a campfire or in a bed. On Boons neglect costs nothing, and staying fed, watered and rested in a bed or by a fire gives bonuses; on Casual, unmet needs only drain some stamina (never more than half) and it comes back once you’ve seen to them; on Hard they cost attributes and health and can make you sick; Off is the classic game.

Windmills with turning sails on seven farms, with machinery inside and a look for every climate and season. Off leaves the farms as they were.
Needs the Improved Interior Lighting mod. Its warm, flickering lights replace the classic lighting, and with shadows on, lamps, people and monsters cast soft shadows too.
With the Morrowind body, bodies and horses stand as flat upright pictures, like the classic sprites. Off, they are drawn as the camera sees them in 3D.
In third person a Morrowind body walks at the pace you move, carries each weapon its own way, and swings with its whole body while its legs keep moving. Off plays Morrowind’s own animations.
With the Morrowind body, Pixelated draws bodies, horses and your arms in large pixels like the classic sprites. Sharp draws them at your screen’s full resolution and uses more video memory.
Takes effect at once; Ship handling, the next time you take the helm. Online it is always on.

Ship battles on Come Sail Away’s boats: at the helm, look to one side and hold Attack to aim a broadside, then let go to fire. Pirates, merchant ships and navies sail the Bay; batter a ship until it surrenders, board it, take its cargo, then sink it or let it go. Piracy is a crime, and pirates can board your ship and fight you on deck. Online, everyone in the room shares one sea.
The screen pulses as your health gets low: slowly below 40%, fast below 20%. On by default in Daggerfall Unity.

With Morrowind People on, a small icon bobs over the people worth finding: a yellow mark over someone a quest needs, a coin over a merchant, and a blue gem over guild trainers, guild quest givers and the arena’s officers.
A notice slides in when a quest begins, when its journal gains an entry, when one of its deadlines is less than a day away, and when it ends. Off updates the journal without a notice.
Places your quests send you to are marked on the map once your map knows them, and the quest you follow is marked on the compass. Off is the classic map and compass, which mark nothing for a quest.

A card at the top right shows the quest you track from the journal, or else the one it last updated: its newest entry, where it points and the time left. Off keeps the classic screen, with no quest card.
Takes effect on the next quest you take; quests you already have keep the rules they began with.

Every quest shows its objectives, some let you choose how they end, some offer a piece of gear fitted to you when done, and questlines lead to the Breaches, the Battlespire and the Abyss. Off is the classic journal and its rewards, and online it is always on.

Loot without opening a window: the mouse wheel moves through the list, Activate takes one item, and the Take everything key takes all but junk (Take gear sets which gear). Off uses the inventory window.

Diamond puts 4 slots in a diamond at the bottom left, on keys 1 to 4. Hotbar puts 10 above your health bars on keys 1 to 0; Diamonds makes them diamonds. Drag an item or spell onto a slot, or point at it and press the key. Off hides them, but their keys still work.

Trees grow together in forests, with open grassland between them. Dungeons, ruins, shrines and camps are often hidden in the woods, and towns and farms stand in cleared fields. Deserts are unchanged. Off spreads the trees evenly, like the original.

Draws the world at a lower resolution and scales it up to fit; menus and the HUD stay sharp. Try 75% if the outdoors run slow on a big or high-resolution screen. Retro Picture Mode replaces this while it is on.

How herbs, veins, trees and other gathering spots near you stand out. Glint makes them catch the light with sparkles; Outline rings each one in its profession’s color, plain to see day or night; Both does both.
Takes effect on the next dungeon you enter. A save made at the other size puts you at the dungeon’s start.

Dungeons bigger than five blocks are cut down to five: a center block with four around it, the same every visit. Main-story dungeons keep full size; a quest keeps the size it was set up at. Online every dungeon has its own size instead.
Takes effect at once; new characters and shop stock follow it.
Your light in dungeons comes from a torch, lantern or candle you carry, and it burns down, instead of a light you always have. Off by default in Daggerfall Unity.

Random monsters are picked from the dungeon’s full list around your level, so a dungeon has more variety instead of the same few. Off by default in Daggerfall Unity.

How detailed the enhanced water is. Full shows what lies under the surface and ripples where things move; Simple is lighter on your machine.
A weapon with a fire, frost or shock damage bonus wears a moving outline of its element, brighter the stronger it is, and an enchanted Morrowind weapon glows. Off draws weapons as before.
Rain, storms and snow move across the land with the wind, so you can see a storm coming, walk into it and out the other side. Off uses the classic weather, the same everywhere in the region.
Out in the wilds you sometimes meet a small group of enemies, a camp or a roaming pack, instead of only one at a time. Off keeps the classic single encounters.

Everyone plays their own save, and you can see and talk to each other anywhere. Dungeons and buildings are shared: enemies, doors, levers and opened chests are the same for everyone and stay that way. In towns and the wilds, everyone nearby sees the same monsters and can fight them, and they can hurt you too. {skyDay} The world’s clock and sky run on real time. Resting, travel, jail and training don’t move them, so a quest waiting for a time of day waits for the world’s, and a lycanthrope’s full moon lasts one night. Your character also has their own clock. It runs while you play and stops while you are logged off. Resting, travel, jail and training use it. Your wounds, spells, hunger, diseases, curses, guild ranks, rented rooms, loans and repairs run on it. Quest timers run on the world’s clock while you play. Resting, waiting and traveling don’t use up a quest’s days, and time logged off never counts. A quest that only asks you to wait, like a letter or “come back in a few days”, moves on after a couple of minutes of play. Rest at a fire, a tent or a bed: a night passes at once, at most once every 10 minutes of play, and party members within 15 meters sleep with you. With a Fishing-Net in your pack, fish while standing or swimming in water, or aboard a ship, at any hour. Hold the use key to draw back and release to cast. When the floats dip, press it again. Then hold to raise the band and release to lower it, keeping the net's weight inside the band to fill the net. Cast at a rising school for an extra fish.

Press the use key at a patch of herbs in the wilderness. Common herbs need no tool; the rest need a Sickle in your pack. With a Basket, the patch's list also lets you search it for food. The Sickle and the Basket can be used from your hotbar or quick slots as well. Used from your pack, a tool only tells you where it can be used.

With a Skinning Knife in your pack, you can skin a creature you killed. Hold the use key at the start of the line and drag the knife along it. Used from your hotbar or a quick slot, the knife is held for you: follow the line with your eyes. The carcass's list also lets you search it.

Press the use key at a tree in the wilderness. You need a Wood-Axe in your pack. Only some trees in each place can be felled each day. The axe can also be used from your hotbar or quick slots. Used from your pack, a tool only tells you where it can be used.

Press the use key at a vein of ore or a boulder in the wilderness, or at a vein in a dungeon. You need a Pick-Axe in your pack. The pick can also be used from your hotbar or quick slots. Used from your pack, a tool only tells you where it can be used.

Veins hold Silver at most until three different players, each with an account at least a week old, have gathered on that ground. Then Gold, Platinum and Mithril in the mountains, and the region's own ore, can appear. Deep veins in dungeons can hold any of their ores, Dwarven Scrap and Adamantium among them, in any dungeon; only a woodland dungeon's Moonstone waits for three players to gather in it. Point at open ground on the world map to see what its veins hold and whether it has been witnessed yet.
As a {name}, you need no witnesses: your veins can give any ore the land holds. A region's own ore still needs the other players.

Outfitting is done at a loom: a Clothing Store's or one in your own home. Open the Stores page there (Holdings > Stores). The loom's tanning rack cures the hides you skin into leather, the loom weaves Root Tendrils into Linen and spins furs into Wool, and it makes leather armor, clothing, rugs, tapestries and the Fishing-Net.
